source_issues.detail: Learning objectives promise implementing BPE, WordPiece and Unigram, but supplied main.py and lesson build steps implement CharTokenizer/BPETokenizer only; WordPiece is an exercise and no Unigram implementation or sentencepiece-library usage is supplied. Preserved.

Claim that common patterns get short token IDs conflates frequency/compression with ID representation length. The shown BPE allocates merged IDs sequentially (256+i), not by shorter bit-length. Preserved.
Heading says three failed approaches and one winner, while body introduces three approaches, two failing. Both preserved.

Broad claims about no unknown tokens, language-agnostic behavior, multilingual ratios, exact context penalty, throughput and fairness depend on vocabulary, preprocessing, implementation, text and hardware. Frozen claims retained without live verification.
Fenced BPE worked example contains an explicitly retracted intermediate (e,s) merge after (w,e); entire explanatory payload remains untouched as required.
Model vocabulary sizes and averages conflate ordinary mergeable vocabulary, special/reserved IDs and vocabulary upper bounds; numbers are preserved and not live-verified.

Source sentence about every BERT variant is syntactically interrupted before the RoBERTa BPE caveat. Translation keeps the interruption and caveat rather than silently inventing a complete universal claim.
128,000*4,096=524,288,000 and 32,000*4,096=131,072,000, a difference of 393,216,000. Source 524/131 million and 400M are rounded; retained.
Vocabulary growth 256+num_merges holds only if training completes every requested merge; code exits early if no pairs remain.

Toy byte-level tokenizer falls back to bytes, not generally Unicode characters; ASCII example hides distinction. Production tiktoken also has regex pre-tokenization and special-token handling beyond the toy algorithm. Exact-same-algorithm claim and simplified 100,000 merges retained.
